chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad Al-Kinani, from someone else, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding in how many garments the woman is shrouded. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She is shrouded in five garments, one of them being the headscarf.'
ai.seo_question: How many garments are used to shroud a woman in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi establishes the standard five-piece shroud for women, with the khimar (headscarf) explicitly designated as a distinct garment, reflecting the Shia emphasis on modesty in death mirroring life. This ruling is often discussed in contrast to the three-piece shroud for men, highlighting the specific legal considerations for female burial rites in Ja'fari jurisprudence.
